sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Connecticut, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Monday, November 2Passed

The deadline to ask for an absentee ballot for the November 3, 2026 election is Monday, November 2, 2026. Ballots have been issued since October 2. Because the ballot must be back by 8 p.m. on Election Day, a late request leaves little time to mail it back; you can also return it in person or by drop box. Within 6 days of the election, use the emergency application. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your absentee ballot must be received by your Town Clerk by the close of polls, 8 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A postmark is not enough. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Sunday, November 1, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Connecticut’s own site

At school away from home, in Connecticut or in another state? What Connecticut says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. A 2026 state law (Public Act 26-42), carrying out the result of the November 2024 statewide vote, means any active registered voter may ask for an absentee ballot without giving a reason. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Apply on the Secretary of the State's online absentee ballot request portal. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Download the Application for Absentee Ballot (form ED-3, in English and Spanish), fill it in, and mail it to the Town Clerk in the town where you live. Giving a phone number or email helps the clerk reach you if your envelope needs fixing. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Hand deliver the paper application to your Town Clerk, or pick one up at the Town Clerk's office. Within 6 days of the election, use the Emergency Application for Absentee Ballot. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it to your Town Clerk by U.S. mail in the return envelope that came with your ballot. It must arrive by 8 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)
  • Drop box. Put it in your town's secure ballot drop box (usually outside town hall). Ask your Town Clerk where it is. (official page)
  • In person. Take it to your Town Clerk's office. Only you, an immediate family member who lives with you, or a person caring for you if you are ill or disabled (such as a doctor or nurse) may return it, or a town police officer or a registrar of voters. (official page)

What the envelope needs

The state's pages ask for no witness or notary. Print your name and sign your name on the outside of the return envelope (Connecticut now uses one envelope; a privacy sleeve is optional). If your signature is missing, the Town Clerk will try to reach you by phone or email, and you can fix it in person at the Town Clerk's office until 8 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Connecticut’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Monday, October 19, 2026 to Sunday, November 1, 2026.

Anyone can vote early in person at their town's early voting location from Monday, October 19 through Sunday, November 1, 2026: 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. most days, and 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Tuesday, October 27 and Thursday, October 29. You can also register and vote the same day at the early voting location. (official page)

Students

At school in Connecticut, away from home

The state's student fact sheet says you can vote either in your hometown or in the town where you live while at college. Where you physically live, not your mailing address, decides where you vote; courts have said you are a resident of a town you have a real tie to and intend to return to. To vote in your hometown while at school, apply for a Connecticut absentee ballot online or on paper. (official page)

At school in another state, with Connecticut as home

A Connecticut student going to college elsewhere can vote in their hometown by applying for a Connecticut absentee ballot (online or on paper). Students from other states going to college in Connecticut can vote either in their home state or in the Connecticut town where they live at college; each state has its own deadlines, so check with your home state's election officials. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military and overseas voters can ask for a ballot with Connecticut's absentee ballot application or the federal FPCA (one FPCA covers the primary and general election for the year), and can choose to get the ballot by email. A completed application may be faxed or emailed to your Town Clerk, as long as the signed original comes back with your voted ballot by the close of polls on Election Day (8 p.m., November 3, 2026). The federal write-in ballot (FWAB) is a backup and must also arrive by the close of polls. (official page)

Connecticut in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The state's Student Voter Fact Sheet still lists the old reasons for an absentee ballot (such as being away from town on Election Day). The state's main absentee page says that since Public Act 26-42 no reason is needed, so we follow that page.
  • If you return an absentee ballot and then want to vote in person on Election Day, you must first go to your town clerk's office before 10 a.m. on Election Day to withdraw the absentee ballot.
  • The state's military and overseas page says it is being updated; questions can go to the Secretary of the State's office.

How this was checked

  • The Federal Voting Assistance Program page loads by script and could not be read; it is linked, not quoted.
